strip.label: Share of the identified savings by finding

facts.evidence: every one opens to its evidence

findings.note: Each saving is measured minus counterfactual over the runs it cites, at the price each call actually paid. Evidence opens the runs and the arithmetic behind every number, and Fix opens the change that removes it.
findings.empty: No open finding matches the supported patterns in the available data. Missing usage or prices can prevent a cost estimate.

kindDefinition.cache_writes_never_read: A run wrote a prompt cache that no later request read.
kindDefinition.duplicate_tool_calls: Every tool call in the request repeated an earlier call in the run with the same input and the same result.
kindDefinition.repeated_shell_commands: Every shell command in the request repeated an earlier command in the run with the same input and the same result.
kindDefinition.unpaged_results: A tool returned more than 20,000 tokens in one result where a 4,000-token page would do.
kindDefinition.spin_loops: An agent repeated the same call 20 or more times in a row in one run and got the same result each time.
kindDefinition.standing_context: Every request in a run re-read the same prefix of system prompt, tool definitions, and steering.
kindDefinition.idle_cache_rewrites: A request after an idle gap longer than the cache lifetime wrote the whole prefix again.
kindDefinition.cache_busts: A change near the top of the prefix made a request write the whole cache again with no idle gap.
kindDefinition.model_class_fit: A run that changed no file is repriced on a smaller model class as an estimate.
kindDefinition.repeated_instructions: The same instruction reached 3 or more runs as prompt text instead of as a steering record.
kindDefinition.recurring_runs: A run started with the same prompt as 4 or more other runs, made no mutating call, and changed no file.
kindDefinition.spend_with_no_outcome: A run ended with nothing kept because its PR closed unmerged, its change was reverted, or it stopped mid-step.

fix.title: Review the recommended change
fix.body: Review the recommendation before changing instructions, a harness, or a tool. Recording a fix only updates this finding. It does not edit code, open a pull request, or measure realised savings.

fix.contextBody: For an instruction or workflow change, review the finding and recommendation in the context-record wizard. Nothing is published until you review and merge its pull request.
fix.codeBody: Review a request for stella to inspect the finding and plan a harness hook, custom tool, or code change. Opening a pull request depends on the repository tools and access available to stella.
fix.effort: Implementation cost is not estimated. Potential savings exclude the cost of making the change.
fix.codeAction: Plan a code PR with stella
fix.codeDraft:
Inspect this spend finding and read the cited calls before proposing a change. Plan the smallest harness hook, custom tool, or code fix that addresses the behavior, with tests. Separate measured costs from potential savings. Estimate implementation cost only with stated assumptions. Open a reviewable code PR only if repository tools and access are available. Otherwise report the missing access. Do not mark the finding fixed.

dialog.title: Set a negotiated rate
dialog.body: Fill in the classes your contract names. Each one is written as its own effective-dated row, in the order below, under the one date you give. A rate you set beats the provider list price for that model and class from that date on; the row it supersedes is closed and kept, so a run priced earlier keeps the rate it was priced with.
dialog.aliasesHint: Separate them with commas. Leave it empty to keep the names already stored.
dialog.effectiveFromHint: A UTC day, tomorrow or later. Leave it empty to start now. A rate cannot start in the past: runs already priced keep the rate they were priced with.
dialog.rates: Rates in US dollars per million units
dialog.ratesHint: Type the figure the way your contract reads it: 2.40 is $2.40 per million. Leave a class empty to leave it as it is.

errors.providerInvalid: Enter the vendor’s name, up to 128 characters.
errors.modelInvalid: Enter the model id, up to 256 characters.
errors.regionInvalid: A region is at most 64 characters.
errors.aliasesInvalid: Enter up to 32 names, each at most 256 characters.
errors.effectiveFromInvalid: Enter a day as YYYY-MM-DD, or leave it empty to start now.
errors.tokenClassInvalid: That is not a token class the price book prices.
errors.rateInvalid: Enter US dollars per one million units, with at most six decimal places.
errors.ratesEmpty: Fill in at least one class. Nothing was written.

partial.written: In effect now: {classes}. Setting a class again supersedes its own row.
partial.noneWritten: Nothing was written. The price book is unchanged.
partial.notWritten: Not written: {classes}. Those classes are still priced as they were.

remove.label: Remove the negotiated rate for {model} ({class})
remove.title: Fall back to the list price
remove.body: Ending your negotiated rate for {model}, {class} means every call from now on is priced at the provider’s list price instead. Nothing is deleted.
remove.kept: The row is closed at this instant and kept, so a run priced before now still names the rate it was priced with. You can negotiate the class again at any time.
remove.submit: End the rate and use the list price
remove.unpriced: Your negotiated rate for {model}, {class} is ended. No list or override price covers this model and class, so calls from now on are UNPRICED, not priced at the list rate, until you set a new rate or a catalog publishes one.
remove.confirmUnpriced: No list or override price covers {model}, {class}. Ending your negotiated rate now, rather than setting a new one first, leaves every call from now on UNPRICED, not priced at the list rate, until you set one.
remove.confirmUnpricedSubmit: End the rate and leave it unpriced
remove.cancelScheduled: Cancel this scheduled rate. The preceding rate continues until the next scheduled rate, if any. Later scheduled rates stay in place.
